cards.heading: Galaxy spin parity — a measurement, and a doubt
cards.body: A pre-registered test of whether an apparent handedness excess is in the sky, or in the people who classified it. NebulaMind Lab.

cards.heading: Published studies disagree about the same galaxies
cards.body: If the universe carried a preferred handedness, spiral galaxies would show it. Some published analyses claim exactly that signal; others find the same excess is an artifact of how people labelled the images.

cards.heading: So the rules were frozen before the first row was fetched
cards.body: Every cut, every threshold, and the bar a reversal had to clear were fixed in a contract before any data was pulled. The measurement then returned a clear and strongly significant reading — and this lane still cannot tell you what it means, because the archive never states the one convention the answer turns on. That is the story.
classified galaxies in the source catalogue. Independently re-parsed by a second seat, which reproduced every funnel count exactly and found zero duplicate identifiers.

cards.heading: Every cut was declared in advance, and the counts survive each one
cards.body: Counts at each rung. 29,053 ties at the flag rung; none at the dominance rungs, where a tie is structurally impossible.

cards.heading: The columns were checked before they were trusted
cards.body: 36 of 36 probed objects aligned, and none crossed. The one error that did surface was in our own frozen contract: a known classifier bias recorded backwards.

cards.heading: Mirroring the images moves the asymmetry to the other side of zero
cards.body: The asymmetry per condition, with its error bar. Normal and the monochrome control sit one side of zero; both mirror sets sit the other, at both rungs.

cards.heading: A mirror should not change the sky
cards.body: So this is a reading about the bias-study sample and the people who labelled the images — not a cosmological asymmetry, not a dipole, not a parity result. That fence was drawn before the measurement.

cards.heading: The separation clears a bar frozen before any data was seen
cards.body: The rule was fixed before a single row was fetched: a reversal had to clear three sigma. Every cell clears it by more than twice, using the conservative error rather than the favourable one.

cards.heading: Not one object kept its label
cards.body: A second gated measurement paired the same galaxies object by object. Of those clearly classified in both conditions, every single one changed label. The pre-registered reading is MIXED — the flip is total, its imbalance sits just above its bar.

cards.heading: But what the mirror does not explain stays under two sigma
cards.body: The flip is real, but the mirrored magnitude is smaller than a perfect mirror predicts. The leftover is under 2 sigma from zero everywhere — a coherent hint, not a fact.

cards.heading: We suspected our own result, and tested it
cards.body: A perfect flip looked mechanical, as if one column had been derived from another. Four checks on the pinned data refuted it: the vote totals are independent, the values scatter like separate draws, and the coincidence that raised the alarm held for a count, never for the objects.

cards.heading: The same numbers support opposite conclusions
cards.body: The result depends on a convention neither primary source states: whether the archived directions were recorded as the classifier saw them, or corrected back first. Both papers were fetched and read. Neither says. So what this measurement means is undetermined.

cards.heading: And the source paper reports the opposite
cards.body: On data of the same provenance, the original study found no reversal. We found one. That is unexplained. A gated measurement of per-object flips is drafted to test whether our cut selects different galaxies rather than different behaviour.

cards.heading: A pre-registered “undetermined” is still an answer
cards.body: Because the rules were frozen first, this reading cannot be a conclusion picked after the numbers were seen. What the lane can state is exactly where the measurement stops: the flip is real in the data, its meaning is not recoverable from the archive as published, and the next gated test is already drafted.

cards.heading: nebulamind.net
cards.body: A record of work in progress. Published because a lane that catches its own error is worth as much as one that finishes.
